title: TypeScript Intermediate: Utility Types, Narrowing & Advanced Types
description: Go beyond the basics: compose types with Partial, Pick, Omit & Record, narrow unknown values safely with type guards and predicates, build mapped and template literal types, constrain and default generics, write function overloads, and use satisfies to keep precise inference.

lessons.title: Utility Types: Partial, Pick, Omit & Record

questions.prompt: What does `Omit<Task, 'id'>` produce?
options: A copy of Task with only id

questions.prompt: The utility type that makes every property of an existing type optional is ____.
Record<K, V> requires K to be a string, number, or symbol (or a union of them).
Which utility type keeps only the listed keys of an existing type?
Task['priority'] reads the type of Task's priority property directly off the interface.

lessons.title: Type Narrowing: unknown, Guards & Predicates

questions.prompt: What's the key difference between unknown and any?
options: unknown must be narrowed before use, any bypasses type checking entirely
questions.answer: unknown must be narrowed before use, any bypasses type checking entirely

questions.prompt: A function with return type 'value is Task' is a custom type predicate.
The operator used to narrow a union by checking whether a property exists on an object is ____.
Which keyword narrows a union to a specific class instance?
A custom type predicate is checked for logical correctness by the compiler, so a wrong one is impossible to write.

lessons.title: Mapped & Template Literal Types

questions.prompt: ____ Task produces a union of all of Task's property names.
What does the [K in keyof Task] syntax do inside a mapped type?
options: Loops over each of Task's property names, building one new property per key
questions.answer: Loops over each of Task's property names, building one new property per key

questions.prompt: Partial<T> and Readonly<T> are implemented internally as mapped types.
What does `${Priority}Changed` produce when Priority is 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'?
options: A union of one literal per member: 'lowChanged' | 'mediumChanged' | 'highChanged'
questions.answer: A union of one literal per member: 'lowChanged' | 'mediumChanged' | 'highChanged'

questions.prompt: The built-in intrinsic type that uppercases the first letter of a string literal type is ____.

lessons.title: The satisfies Operator & Const Assertions

questions.prompt: What does satisfies do that a plain type annotation does not?
options: Checks the value against a type while keeping its own precise inferred type
Converts the value to that type at runtime
questions.answer: Checks the value against a type while keeping its own precise inferred type

questions.prompt: as const widens an array literal's type to string[].
typeof someArray[number] extracts a union type of the array's ____.
Without `as const`, what type does `['up', 'down']` infer to?
satisfies and as const solve the same problem and are interchangeable.

lessons.title: Generic Constraints & Default Type Parameters

questions.prompt: What does `T extends HasId` mean for a generic type parameter?
options: T must be a subclass of HasId
Whatever T is, it must have at least the shape of HasId
T is ignored at compile time
questions.answer: Whatever T is, it must have at least the shape of HasId

questions.prompt: `K extends keyof T` restricts K to only the actual property names of T.
In `interface ApiResponse<T = unknown>`, `unknown` is the ____ type parameter, used when the caller supplies none.
Given `getProperty<T, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, key: K): T[K]`, what does the return type T[K] guarantee?
options: It returns exactly the type of the specific property that was requested
It returns the whole object T
questions.answer: It returns exactly the type of the specific property that was requested

lessons.title: Function Overloads & Call Signatures

questions.prompt: In a set of function overloads, which signature do callers actually see and get checked against?
options: Only the overload signatures, not the implementation signature
All of them, merged into one
questions.answer: Only the overload signatures, not the implementation signature

questions.prompt: An interface can describe something that is both callable and has properties, using a call signature.
The signature with a function body, which every overload must be compatible with, is called the ____ signature.

lessons.title: Final Project: Build a Typed Settings Validator
lessons.content:
# Final Project: Build a Typed Settings Validator

Combine utility types, narrowing, mapped/template literal types, and `satisfies` into one small but real module: a settings validator.

## Requirements

1. Define a `Settings` interface with at least four fields of mixed types (e.g. `theme: 'light' | 'dark'`, `fontSize: number`, `autoSave: boolean`, `username: string`).
2. Write an `isSettings(value: unknown): value is Settings` type predicate that validates an untrusted value (e.g. something parsed from `JSON.parse`) before it's ever treated as `Settings`.
3. Write an `updateSettings(current: Settings, changes: Partial<Settings>): Settings` function, changes should be optional and partial, not a full replacement.
4. Use a mapped type to derive a `SettingsChanged` type, `{ [K in keyof Settings]: boolean }`, and a function that compares two `Settings` objects and returns one, flagging exactly which fields differ.
5. Build a `defaultSettings` object typed with `satisfies Settings`, so each default value keeps its own precise type instead of being widened to a single union.

## Stretch goals

- Add a template literal type deriving an event name per settings key, e.g. `on` + the capitalized key + `Change`, and a tiny typed event emitter that only accepts those names.
- Use `Pick`/`Omit` to derive a "public settings" type that hides one internal-only field from an exported API.
- Add a `resetSettings(): Settings` that returns a fresh copy of `defaultSettings`, and verify at the type level that `defaultSettings` itself can't be mutated by accident.

Submit your repository link below when you are done, an instructor will review it before you can mark this lesson complete. Good luck! 🚀
